headline: Agent Autoloop：让命令行 Agent 后台接活
summary_md: Agent Autoloop is a lightweight, self-hosted automation hub for command-line coding agents like Claude Code and Codex. It lets an agent run in the background, handle events (cron jobs, GitHub issues, alerts), and only interrupt you when it needs a decision — via Slack, Discord, or desktop notifications. The core has zero external dependencies, runs on a single Mac or Linux machine, and uses pluggable sources, agents, and notification channels. Per the README, you can set up rules in a JSON file, and the agent communicates results in its final reply. The project is MIT-licensed and already has 2.3k stars, though its growth rate is unusually high for being only a day old. The product opportunity is a hosted version: a web UI to configure rules, Slack integration, managed execution, and cost/approval tracking. This could appeal to indie hackers and small teams who want reliable, always-on agent workflows without managing infrastructure. The main risks are unverified maturity (Windows support pending, examples not fully tested in real services) and the need to adapt China-centric examples (Feishu, DingTalk) to US/global channels like Slack and Discord. With a clear pain point and permissive license, it's a solid base for a lightweight hosted service, but validation and localization are essential before investing heavily.
title_en: Agent Autoloop: Background CLI Agents That Ask Before Risky Moves
tagline_en: Let your CLI agent pick up tasks and follow through in the background, pinging you only when it's unsure.
